mainTopic: An עירוב on a grave for a כהן, the dispute of רבי יהודה and the רבנן, and which foods may be used for an עירוב
overview: The amud opens with רבי יהודה's view that a pure כהן may have an עירוב made of pure תרומה placed on a grave. The גמרא solves the practical problems one by one. The כהן travels inside a large wooden box. The food never received הכשר, so it cannot become impure. He picks it up with a flat wooden utensil, held sideways so it forms no אהל. Then the גמרא asks why the רבנן still forbid it, and answers that one may not acquire a שבת home with איסורי הנאה. It tries several ways to explain the dispute without making the rules of רבא (מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו) or רב יוסף (an עירוב only for a מצוה) depend on one side of a מחלוקת תנאים. It ends by saying the argument is only about whether a person wants his עירוב food guarded after it has done its job. A new משנה then lists which foods may and may not be used for an עירוב. The גמרא explains that דמאי works through a מיגו: he could make himself poor, and a poor person may eat דמאי. Its proof from a משנה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An עירוב of pure תרומה may be placed on a grave for a pure כהן
steps.stepSummary: The base ruling: a pure כהן can have his עירוב made with pure תרומה that rests on a grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may make an עירוב for a pure כהן with pure תרומה that is placed on a grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ruling that a pure כהן may have his עירוב made from pure תרומה placed on top of a grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is רבי יהודה's position from the משנה, which the רבנן reject. It is surprising: a כהן is forbidden to become impure from a grave, and תרומה may only be eaten while pure. The next steps check how this ruling can work in practice, and step 10 then asks why the רבנן still disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: We make an עירוב (here, an עירוב תחומין: food placed to set a new שבת home base)
A כהן who is ritually pure
Pure תרומה, the כהן's food portion, which only a pure כהן may eat
A grave, which gives off טומאת מת

phrases.english: We may make an eiruv for a pure kohen
phrases.notes: An עירוב must be food that the person it is made for is allowed to eat.

phrases.english: with pure teruma that is on a grave,
phrases.notes: The food is fine for him, but its location is a place he may not enter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְעָרְבִין לְכֹהֵן טָהוֹר בִּתְרוּמָה טְהוֹרָה בְּקֶבֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion here.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a valid עירוב for a pure כהן may consist of pure תרומה placed on a grave (the רבנן forbid it).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an עירוב can be valid even when it sits somewhere the person cannot easily reach, as long as there is some permitted way to get to it.

steps.title: How does the כהן get to the grave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the כהן can reach his עירוב without becoming impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he go there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question: a כהן may not walk up to a grave, so how could he reach his עירוב? It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב only works if the food is reachable and usable in principle. If the כהן had no permitted way to get to it, the ruling in step 1 would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: How?
Does he go

phrases.english: How does he go there?
phrases.notes: He's asking how this could even work in practice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the ruling in step 1 can be carried out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A way for the כהן to reach the grave without becoming impure.

steps.title: He travels inside a large wooden box
steps.stepSummary: He goes inside a שידה, תיבה, or מגדל, which shields him from the טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a carriage, a crate, or a cupboard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the כהן travels inside a large closed wooden container, which shields him from the grave's impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are large wooden containers. Because of their size, they do not become impure themselves, and they block the טומאה from reaching the person inside. So the כהן can get to the grave while staying pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A large closed wooden carriage or box
A crate or chest
A cupboard or tower-shaped cabinet

phrases.english: In a carriage, a crate, or a cupboard.
phrases.notes: All three are large wooden containers that act as a protective barrier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He travels inside a large wooden container that blocks the טומאה.

steps.title: Wouldn't the תרומה itself become impure on the grave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: once the תרומה is placed on the grave, it should become impure and unfit to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But once it was placed down there, it became impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling: food set on a grave should become impure, and impure תרומה cannot be eaten at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first problem was about the כהן. This one is about the food. An עירוב must be food the person may eat, and impure תרומה is forbidden even to a כהן, so the עירוב should be invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, the opening word of a challenge
That it was put down
It became impure

phrases.english: But once it was put down there, it became impure!
phrases.notes: 'Put down' means placed directly on the grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new problem with the ruling of step 1, now about the food itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 1 that the תרומה on the grave stays pure and edible.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food placed on a grave contracts טומאת מת. Impure תרומה is forbidden to eat, and an עירוב must be edible for its owner.

steps.title: The food was never made able to become impure
steps.stepSummary: The תרומה was never wetted by a liquid that brings הכשר, or the dough was kneaded with fruit juice, so it cannot become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where it was not made susceptible, or where it was kneaded with fruit juice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this תרומה cannot become impure at all, because it never touched one of the liquids that make food able to receive impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become impure after it has been wet by one of the seven special liquids, such as water, wine, or oil. This is called הכשר. Either the food was never wet, or it was kneaded with fruit juice, which is not one of the seven. Either way, it stays pure even on a grave.

keyTerms.meaning: Was made susceptible to טומאה by contact with one of the seven liquids
Was kneaded
Fruit juice, which does not make food susceptible to טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think fruit juice is just 'not wet enough'. The rule is that only seven specific liquids bring הכשר, and fruit juice is not one of them.

phrases.english: Where it was not yet made susceptible,
phrases.notes: It never touched any of the seven liquids.

phrases.english: or where it was kneaded with fruit juice.
phrases.notes: Bread dough made with fruit juice remains unable to become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשֶׁלֹּא הוּכְשְׁרָה, אוֹ שֶׁנִּילּוֹשָׁה בְּמֵי פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ruling refers only to food that cannot become impure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The objection assumed this was ordinary תרומה that can become impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is food without הכשר, which stays pure even on a grave.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches the basic rule of הכשר: dry food, or food wet only by other liquids, cannot become impure.

steps.title: How does he pick up the food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the כהן can take the food off the grave without becoming impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does he bring it?
steps.whatsHappening: The food is pure and the כהן is protected inside his box, but now the גמרא asks how he actually picks it up. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he reaches out with his hand, he would leave his protection and become impure. If he uses an ordinary utensil, the utensil could become impure. He needs a tool that cannot become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings or fetches

phrases.english: And how does he bring it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the עירוב food lying on the grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next practical problem after steps 3 and 5 were solved.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A way to retrieve the food from the grave without becoming impure.

steps.title: He uses flat wooden utensils
steps.stepSummary: Flat wooden utensils cannot become impure, so he uses one to pick up the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: With flat wooden utensils, which do not become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he picks up the food with a flat wooden tool, because such tools cannot become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wooden utensils can only become impure if they have a hollow space that holds things (a בית קיבול). A flat wooden board has no such space, so it stays pure while touching the grave area.

keyTerms.meaning: Flat wooden utensils, with no hollow receptacle
Become impure

phrases.english: With flat wooden utensils
phrases.notes: For example, a flat board or tray without a rim.

phrases.english: which do not become impure.
phrases.notes: Only wooden utensils shaped to hold things inside can become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּפְשׁוּטֵי כְלֵי עֵץ דְּלָא מְקַבְּלִי טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He uses a flat wooden utensil, which cannot become impure.

steps.title: Doesn't the utensil form a covering over the grave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the utensil, held over the grave, forms an אהל and would bring impurity to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it forms a covering over the grave!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer: holding a utensil over the grave means it covers the grave like a tent, which would make the כהן holding it impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The utensil itself stays pure, but there is a separate problem. The חכמים decreed that a person holding an object a טפח wide over a grave becomes impure, because the object acts as a tent over the grave. So the flat utensil seems to defeat its purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Forms an אהל, a tent-like covering, over the טומאה
Is doing, an Aramaic word stressing an ongoing action

phrases.english: But it forms a covering over it!
phrases.notes: A covering of a טפח or more over a grave passes on impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the solution given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of a flat wooden utensil to retrieve the food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if the utensil itself stays pure, holding it over a grave forms an אהל, so the person holding it becomes impure.

steps.title: He holds the utensil sideways
steps.stepSummary: He brings the food on the utensil's edge, holding it sideways so it never covers a טפח over the grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings it on its edge, held sideways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he holds the utensil sideways and brings the food on its edge, so it never forms a covering over the grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אהל only exists when there is a covering a טפח wide. A utensil turned on its side presents only a thin edge over the grave, so no אהל is formed. All the problems are now solved, and the ruling from step 1 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Its back or edge, meaning the utensil held sideways

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that you may make an עירוב of pure תרומה on a grave for a pure כהן survives four problems. He reaches it in a large wooden box. The food has no הכשר. He uses a flat wooden utensil. He holds it sideways so it does not form an אהל.

phrases.english: He brings it on its edge, held sideways.
phrases.notes: Holding it sideways means there is no handbreadth-wide covering over the grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 and closes the chain of practical questions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical method: changing how the utensil is held.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The objection assumed the utensil is held flat, covering the grave.
steps.terutzMaskana: Held sideways, the utensil forms no אהל, so the כהן stays pure.

steps.title: So why do the רבנן forbid it?
steps.stepSummary: Since every practical problem has been solved, the גמרא asks what reason the רבנן still have to forbid the עירוב on a grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the רבנן still forbid a כהן's עירוב on a grave, now that the purity problems are solved. This sets up a new answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3-9 showed that the כהן can reach the grave and retrieve the food without becoming טמא, and that the תרומה stays pure. So the רבנן's objection cannot be about טומאה. There must be a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if what was just said is true)
What is the reason?
The Sages (the majority opinion in the משנה)

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: If the כהן really can safely get his pure תרומה off the grave

phrases.english: what is the reason of the Sages?
phrases.notes: Why do they forbid this עירוב?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the solution in step 9 and asks what reason the רבנן have left.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason the רבנן forbid an עירוב on a grave once purity concerns are removed.

steps.title: No acquiring a home with forbidden-benefit items
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that one may not acquire a home with something forbidden for benefit. A grave is such an item.
steps.simpleTranslation: They hold: It is forbidden to acquire a home with items forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the רבנן's problem is not טומאה. Their problem is that a grave is forbidden for benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב makes its location your 'home' for שבת. Using a grave to gain that home counts as benefiting from an איסור הנאה. So even a completely pure עירוב there is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold (their reasoning is)
To acquire a home (here: a שבת residence through an עירוב)
Items one is forbidden to benefit from

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is buying a real house. 'Acquiring a home' means establishing a שבת base through the עירוב.

phrases.english: They hold: It is forbidden to acquire a home
phrases.notes: A שבת residence acquired through the עירוב

phrases.english: with items forbidden for benefit.
phrases.notes: A grave is forbidden for benefit

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן forbid acquiring a שבת residence by means of an איסור הנאה, such as a grave.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה permit using forbidden items?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רבי יהודה must hold it is permitted to acquire a home with איסורי הנאה, and asks whether that is really his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that imply that רבי יהודה holds it is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference: if the רבנן forbid it, רבי יהודה seems to permit it. It asks whether that is truly his position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permitting benefit from איסורי הנאה sounds very surprising. So the גמרא wants to know how רבי יהודה could hold this.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference / this implies
The תנא who permits the עירוב on the grave
Permitted

phrases.english: Does this imply that Rabbi Yehuda
holds it is permitted?
phrases.notes: Permitted to acquire a home with איסורי הנאה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference about רבי יהודה from the רבנן's reason in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, and why, רבי יהודה would permit acquiring a home with איסורי הנאה.

steps.title: Doing a מצוה is not counted as benefit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו. Doing a מצוה is not considered 'benefit,' so using the grave for a מצוה עירוב is no forbidden הנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: מצוות were not given for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה does not allow benefit from forbidden items in general. He holds that doing a מצוה simply does not count as benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב made for a מצוה purpose is not 'enjoyment' in the legal sense. So placing it on a grave is not benefiting from an איסור הנאה. This is an exception based on the purpose of the act. It does not mean איסורי הנאה are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds
מצוות were not given for benefit (doing a מצוה is not counted as personal enjoyment)

steps.whyThisMatters: מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו is a major principle across ש״ס. For example, it lets one fulfill a מצוה with an object one has vowed not to benefit from.

phrases.english: He holds: מצוות were not given for benefit.
phrases.notes: So using a grave for an עירוב, which is a מצוה, isn't forbidden benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה holds מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו, so a מצוה-related עירוב on a grave is not forbidden benefit.

steps.title: Would רבא's rule become just one side of a dispute?
steps.stepSummary: רבא stated מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו as a plain rule. If רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue over it, רבא would be following only one side of a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, regarding what רבא said, 'מצוות were not given for benefit,' shall we say he stated his rule according to one side of a dispute of תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it just gave. It would make רבא's famous rule depend on one side of a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's general rule is normally assumed to fit all the תנאים. If the רבנן reject מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו, רבא's rule would go against the majority view. The גמרא would rather avoid that.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who stated the rule מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו
Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא wants to avoid)
According to (one side of) a dispute of תנאים
His teaching / his halachic rule

phrases.english: But then, that which Rava said:
'מצוות were not given for benefit' —
shall we say he stated his rule according to a dispute of Tannaim?!
phrases.notes: Meaning the רבנן would disagree with him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the consequence of the answer in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רבי יהודה and the רבנן disagree about מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That explanation would turn רבא's general rule into one side of a מחלוקת תנאים, against the רבנן.

steps.title: The real dispute: is an עירוב only for a מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: רבא would answer that everyone agrees מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו. The argument is whether an עירוב may be made only for a מצוה, or also for a voluntary purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא would tell you: If they held that one may make an עירוב only for a מצוה, everyone would agree that מצוות were not given for benefit. But here they argue about this: One master holds one may make an עירוב only for a מצוה, and the other holds one may make an עירוב even for a voluntary matter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא's answer moves the argument to a different question. Both sides accept his rule. They argue over whether an עירוב must be for a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds an עירוב is only for a מצוה. So it is never 'benefit,' and the grave is allowed. The רבנן hold an עירוב may be made even for a personal purpose. That makes it real benefit, so a grave is forbidden. This way רבא's rule stays true for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: He would tell you (the גמרא answers on someone's behalf)
A מצוה purpose
A voluntary, personal purpose
They argue
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: In רבא's version, everyone agrees מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו, and רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue about whether an עירוב must be for a מצוה. Step 16 shows this creates a problem for רב יוסף, and step 17 gives a different account of the dispute.
steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן do not reject מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו. They hold an עירוב can be made for personal reasons, so it is not automatically a מצוה act.

phrases.english: Rava would tell you:
If they held that one does not make an Eiruv
except for a מצוה purpose —
then everyone would agree
that מצוות were not given for benefit.
phrases.notes: So the grave would be permitted by all

phrases.english: But here they argue about this:
One master holds one does not make an Eiruv
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה

phrases.english: except for a מצוה purpose,
and the other master holds one makes an Eiruv
phrases.notes: The רבנן

phrases.english: even for a voluntary purpose.
phrases.notes: So it is real benefit, and a grave is forbidden

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by moving the dispute to a different question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the dispute (אוקימתא of the מחלוקת on a different issue)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue about מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו, so רבא follows only רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree with רבא's rule. They argue whether an עירוב is only for a מצוה (רבי יהודה) or also for a voluntary purpose (רבנן).

steps.title: Would רב יוסף's rule now become a dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The new answer causes the same problem for רב יוסף. He stated as a plain rule that an עירוב is made only for a מצוה, which now looks like רבי יהודה's side alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, regarding what רב יוסף said, 'One makes an עירוב only for a מצוה,' shall we say he stated his rule according to one side of a dispute of תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that saving רבא's rule creates the same problem for רב יוסף's rule. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 made 'an עירוב only for a מצוה' the point of argument. So רב יוסף, who stated it as a general rule, would follow only רבי יהודה against the רבנן. Step 17 gives the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who ruled that an עירוב is made only for a מצוה
One makes an עירוב only for a מצוה purpose

phrases.english: But then, that which Rav Yosef said:
'One makes an Eiruv only for a מצוה purpose' —
shall we say he stated his rule according to a dispute of Tannaim?
phrases.notes: Step 17 gives the answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same challenge as step 14 against the new explanation of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the dispute is over whether an עירוב is made only for a מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That explanation would make רב יוסף's general rule match only רבי יהודה's side of a מחלוקת תנאים.

steps.title: רב יוסף's answer: the argument is about whether he wants the עירוב guarded
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that both sides agree on both rules. They argue only about whether, once the עירוב has acquired his שבת home, he still wants the food protected. If he does, he is getting benefit from the grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף could tell you: Everyone agrees that an עירוב is made only for a מצוה, and everyone agrees that מצות were not given for benefit. They argue about this: One master (רבי יהודה) holds that once the עירוב has acquired his home for him, he does not care whether it is guarded. The other master (the רבנן) holds that he does want it guarded, because if he needs it, he will eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 16 on behalf of רב יוסף. It shows that his rule does not have to belong to only one side of a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now neither רבא's rule nor רב יוסף's rule is in dispute. The whole argument moves to a practical question. Once the עירוב has worked at nightfall (בין השמשות), does the person still care about the food? רבי יהודה says no, so the grave gives him no benefit and the עירוב is allowed. The רבנן say yes, because he may want to eat it later, so keeping the food safe on the grave counts as forbidden benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: He is pleased with it / he wants it
That it is guarded or kept safe
He needs it

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: everyone holds מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו, and everyone holds an עירוב is only for a מצוה. רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue only about whether a person wants his עירוב food protected after it has done its job.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the argument is still about the מצוה itself. The worry is the benefit of keeping the leftover food safe for later. That is a personal benefit, not a מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer lets both רבא and רב יוסף state their rules as plain, agreed rules. Neither one is following only one side of a מחלוקת תנאים.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין מְעָרְבִין אֶלָּא לִדְבַר מִצְוָה,
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that one makes an eruv only for a מצוה,

phrases.aramaic: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִצְוֹת לָאו לֵיהָנוֹת נִיתְּנוּ,
phrases.english: and everyone agrees that מצוות were not given for benefit,
and this is what they argue about:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר כֵּיוָן דִּקְנָה לֵיהּ עֵירוּב —
phrases.english: One master holds: once the eruv has acquired for him [his Shabbos home],
phrases.notes: This master is רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: he does not care that it be guarded.
And the other master holds: he does want it guarded,
phrases.notes: This master is the רבנן.

phrases.english: because if he needs it, he will eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 16 against רב יוסף
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the argument: both rules are agreed, and the dispute is placed on a different, practical point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף's rule that an עירוב is only for a מצוה seemed to follow רבי יהודה alone
steps.terutzMaskana: Both rules are agreed by all. The dispute is whether the person wants the עירוב food guarded after it has worked.

steps.title: New משנה: foods that may be used for an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists foods that may be used for an עירוב: דמאי, first tithe whose תרומה was taken, second tithe and הקדש that were redeemed, and חלה for כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may make an עירוב with דמאי, with first tithe whose תרומה has been taken, with second tithe and הקדש that have been redeemed, and כהנים may use חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists foods that are allowed to be used as an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea behind the list is that the עירוב food must be food the person is allowed to eat. Each item here is food that has been fixed or is permitted, at least for this person. חלה, for example, works for a כהן because a כהן may eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Produce bought from an unlearned person who may not have tithed it
First tithe, given to a לוי, from which the לוי must separate תרומת מעשר
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
Property dedicated to the בית המקדש
A portion of dough given to a כהן

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One may make an eruv with demai,
and with first tithe whose teruma has been taken,
and with second tithe and consecrated items that were redeemed,
and kohanim [may make an eruv] with challah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous sugya ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב may be made with permitted or fixed foods: דמאי, first tithe whose תרומה was taken, redeemed second tithe and הקדש, and חלה for כהנים

steps.title: The משנה continues: foods that may not be used for an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the opposite cases. טבל, first tithe whose תרומה was not taken, and unredeemed second tithe and הקדש may not be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: But not with טבל, not with first tithe whose תרומה has not been taken, and not with second tithe or הקדש that have not been redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list by naming foods that are not allowed for an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item here is the forbidden version of an item from the first list. These foods may not be eaten yet, so they cannot serve as an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומה and tithes have not yet been separated, so it is forbidden to eat
That were not redeemed

phrases.english: But not with tevel,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְּרוּמָתוֹ,
phrases.english: and not with first tithe whose teruma was not taken,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדּוּ.
phrases.english: and not with second tithe and consecrated items that were not redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same משנה, giving the forbidden cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food that is still forbidden to eat (טבל, unfixed first tithe, unredeemed second tithe or הקדש) may not be used for an עירוב

steps.title: How can דמאי work if he may not eat it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's first ruling. דמאי is forbidden to eat until it is tithed, so how can it be used for an עירוב?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: דמאי? But it is not fit for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the very first item in the משנה. It asks how דמאי can be an עירוב when the person is not allowed to eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב must be food that is fit for the person. A regular person may not eat דמאי until he takes off the tithes. So the משנה seems to break the basic rule of עירוב food.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
It is not fit for him

phrases.english: GEMARA: Demai?
But it is not fit for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first ruling of the משנה in Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one may make an עירוב with דמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עירוב must be food fit for the person. דמאי is forbidden to him, so it should not work.

steps.title: The מיגו answer: he could make himself poor
steps.stepSummary: Because he could declare all his property הפקר and become poor, and a poor person may eat דמאי, the דמאי already counts as fit for him now.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since, if he wanted, he could make his property ownerless and become a poor person, and then the דמאי would be fit for him, it counts as fit for him even now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a מיגו: since he could make the דמאי fit for himself, it already counts as fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים allowed poor people to eat דמאי. Anyone can become poor by declaring his property הפקר. Since that option is in his own hands, the food is not truly out of his reach, so it is considered fit for him even though he has not done it.

keyTerms.meaning: Since (he could do X, Y is also true): an argument from what one is able to do
Declares ownerless (הפקר)
A poor person

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not mean he actually has to give away his property. The mere ability to do so is enough for the דמאי to count as fit.

phrases.english: Since, if he wanted,
he could declare his property ownerless
and he would be a poor person, and it would be fit for him,
now too it is fit for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיגּוֹ דְּאִי בָּעֵי מַפְקַר לְהוּ לְנִכְסֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: מיגו: what he is able to do makes the food count as fit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דמאי is forbidden to him, so it cannot be an עירוב
steps.terutzMaskana: Since he could become poor and eat it, the דמאי is considered fit for him now

steps.title: Source: poor people may be fed דמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה as a source that poor people may be fed דמאי. This supports the key fact behind the מיגו.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One may feed the poor דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to prove that a poor person may eat דמאי. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מיגו only works if poor people really are allowed to eat דמאי. This משנה gives that rule a clear written source.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
One may feed

phrases.english: As we learned: One may feed the poor demai,
phrases.notes: The quotation continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the fact used in Step 21's מיגו
steps.raayaObject: That a poor person is permitted to eat דמאי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (דמאי פרק ג) teaching that one may feed the poor דמאי
